definition: Cascading means passing along in a chain, with each stage setting off the next.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cascading. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cascading should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One rumor about the bank's losses set off a cascading run of withdrawals that spread to three neighboring lenders by Friday.
Rippling is milder than cascading — ripples spread and fade, while a cascading failure gathers force with each stage it topples.
Runaway is stronger than cascading — a cascading failure still moves stage by stage, but a runaway one has stopped answering to any brake at all.

Snowballing trouble grows bigger and faster as it rolls, the way a snowball gathers snow. Cascading is about sequence rather than size: a cascading failure travels stage by stage, each one setting off the next, whether or not the total ever grows huge.

Chain-reaction is the physicist's label for the linked process itself, and it is usually a noun naming the whole event. Cascading is the adjective you attach to the effects as they travel — cascading failures, cascading delays — with each stage directly causing the next.

Escalating trouble is getting more serious or more intense step by step, as a quarrel escalates into a feud. Cascading keeps the focus on cause: each stage directly produces the one after it, whether or not the stakes are rising.

The trouble at the port began with a single crane that failed its morning inspection.
Its berth closed, and the container ship waiting there was sent to the next dock, pushing that dock's scheduled arrival out to sea for a day.
That delayed ship carried parts for two factories inland, which idled their afternoon shifts; the factories' unfilled trucks left grocery warehouses short by the weekend.
Analysts called it a textbook case of cascading disruption: no single stage was large, but each one set off the stage after it.
By the time the crane was repaired, the effects had traveled five steps from the dock without ever growing bigger — only farther.
